items.claim: The row's claim that Eccl.7.9 shares "no repeated phrase" with the double tov-saying before it is contradicted by the shared root ruach ("spirit"), which closes 7:8 twice and opens 7:9's own clause.
items.evidence: oshb:Eccl.7.8 “ט֛וֹב אַחֲרִ֥ית דָּבָ֖ר מֵֽרֵאשִׁית֑וֹ ט֥וֹב אֶֽרֶךְ ר֖וּחַ מִגְּבַהּ רֽוּחַ” (byte tier) carries the ruach root twice; oshb:Eccl.7.9 “אַל תְּבַהֵ֥ל בְּרֽוּחֲךָ֖ לִכְע֑וֹס כִּ֣י כַ֔עַס בְּחֵ֥יק כְּסִילִ֖ים יָנֽוּחַ” (byte tier) repeats the same root (suffixed form) at the verse's own opening clause (sweep: 20 verses book-wide carry the ruach root, with Eccl.7.8 and Eccl.7.9 as consecutive entries) -- an undisclosed catchword straddling the row's own front seam. The atomic single_saying call may still stand on topical grounds (patience vs. anger), but the stated warrant overclaims a total absence of shared vocabulary.
tier_citations: book-wide skeleton sweep of the ruach root: 20 verses

items.claim: device_notes states that 7:10 anticipates the 7:11-7:12 wisdom sayings "without sharing their vocabulary," but 7:10's own prefixed form repeats the very root (chokmah, "wisdom") that opens 7:11 and recurs twice in 7:12.
items.evidence: oshb:Eccl.7.10 “אַל תֹּאמַר֙ מֶ֣ה הָיָ֔ה שֶׁ֤הַיָּמִים֙ הָרִ֣אשֹׁנִ֔ים הָי֥וּ טוֹבִ֖ים מֵאֵ֑לֶּה כִּ֛י לֹ֥א מֵחָכְמָ֖ה שָׁאַ֥לְתָּ עַל זֶֽה” (byte tier) carries the chokmah root (prefixed "from wisdom"); oshb:Eccl.7.11 “טוֹבָ֥ה חָכְמָ֖ה עִֽם נַחֲלָ֑ה וְיֹתֵ֖ר לְרֹאֵ֥י הַשָּֽׁמֶשׁ” and oshb:Eccl.7.12 “כִּ֛י בְּצֵ֥ל הַֽחָכְמָ֖ה בְּצֵ֣ל הַכָּ֑סֶף וְיִתְר֣וֹן דַּ֔עַת הַֽחָכְמָ֖ה תְּחַיֶּ֥ה בְעָלֶֽיהָ” (byte tier) repeat it twice more (sweep: 22 verses book-wide carry the chokmah root, with Eccl.7.10-Eccl.7.12 as three consecutive entries) -- the same root the device_notes calls unshared is this row's own immediate downstream neighbor-token.
tier_citations: book-wide skeleton sweep of the chokmah root: 22 verses

items.claim: The saying_cluster's own front-seam claim -- that 7:11 is held apart from 7:10 on "no shared vocabulary" -- is contradicted by the very root (chokmah, "wisdom") the row treats as its cluster's binding term.
items.evidence: oshb:Eccl.7.10 “אַל תֹּאמַר֙ מֶ֣ה הָיָ֔ה שֶׁ֤הַיָּמִים֙ הָרִ֣אשֹׁנִ֔ים הָי֥וּ טוֹבִ֖ים מֵאֵ֑לֶּה כִּ֛י לֹ֥א מֵחָכְמָ֖ה שָׁאַ֥לְתָּ עַל זֶֽה” and oshb:Eccl.7.11 “טוֹבָ֥ה חָכְמָ֖ה עִֽם נַחֲלָ֑ה וְיֹתֵ֖ר לְרֹאֵ֥י הַשָּֽׁמֶשׁ” (byte tier) share the chokmah root the row's own rationale leans on as the cluster's argument-subject, alongside oshb:Eccl.7.12 “כִּ֛י בְּצֵ֥ל הַֽחָכְמָ֖ה בְּצֵ֣ל הַכָּ֑סֶף וְיִתְר֣וֹן דַּ֔עַת הַֽחָכְמָ֖ה תְּחַיֶּ֥ה בְעָלֶֽיהָ” (byte tier, chokmah root twice more) (sweep: 22 verses book-wide, Eccl.7.10-Eccl.7.12 three consecutive entries). The internal 7:11|7:12 grammatical dependency (the causal "for"-clause) is byte-sound and the cluster call plausibly survives, but the row's stated warrant against merging with 7:10 mischaracterizes the bytes at its own boundary.
tier_citations: book-wide skeleton sweep of the chokmah root: 22 verses

items.claim: admonition_unit is a properly disclosed operative-category deviation for 7:13-7:14: both verses share the imperative root ra'ah ("see/consider") and the root asah ("do/make") naming God's action, a byte-grounded frame the sentence zone's tov-comparative default does not carry.
items.evidence: oshb:Eccl.7.13 “רְאֵ֖ה אֶת מַעֲשֵׂ֣ה הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים כִּ֣י מִ֤י יוּכַל֙ לְתַקֵּ֔ן אֵ֖ת אֲשֶׁ֥ר עִוְּתֽוֹ” and oshb:Eccl.7.14 “בְּי֤וֹם טוֹבָה֙ הֱיֵ֣ה בְט֔וֹב וּבְי֥וֹם רָעָ֖ה רְאֵ֑ה גַּ֣ם אֶת זֶ֤ה לְעֻמַּת זֶה֙ עָשָׂ֣ה הָֽאֱלֹהִ֔ים עַל דִּבְרַ֗ת שֶׁלֹּ֨א יִמְצָ֧א הָֽאָדָ֛ם אַחֲרָ֖יו מְאֽוּמָה” (byte tier) repeat the ra'ah imperative in the same form in both verses, and the asah root (as the noun ma'aseh in 7:13, as the finite verb in 7:14) with ha'elohim as referent in both; neither verse opens on a tov-comparative token (tov-opener sweep: 12 verses book-wide, none at 7:13 or 7:14), so the deviation disclosure is accurate; the row correctly separates from 7:12's wisdom-value cluster (topic shift to direct address) and from 7:15's first-person report (register shift), matching the verified bytes at both boundaries.

items.claim: monologue_unit correctly applies to 7:15 as the M parent's operative default outside the 7:1-14 sentence zone; the row's report-vs-imperative seam against both 7:14 and 7:16 holds at the bytes.
items.evidence: oshb:Eccl.7.15 “אֶת הַכֹּ֥ל רָאִ֖יתִי בִּימֵ֣י הֶבְלִ֑י יֵ֤שׁ צַדִּיק֙ אֹבֵ֣ד בְּצִדְק֔וֹ וְיֵ֣שׁ רָשָׁ֔ע מַאֲרִ֖יךְ בְּרָעָתֽוֹ” (byte tier) opens on the first-person report verb ra'iti ("I have seen"), matching the raiti-observation inventory (sweep: 18 verses book-wide, Eccl.7.15 among them) and distinct from 7:14's imperative forms of ra'ah/hayah and 7:16's imperative form of hayah; no tov-opener or refrain token opens the verse, and the strongest_rejected_alternative (folding into the 7:16-18 counsel) is genuinely engaged and rejected on the same person-shift grounds the bytes support.

items.claim: observed_substrate_signals affirmatively states "no tov-opener... token in this span," but 7:18 itself opens with tov and is one of the strategy's own seven ch-7 tov-opener sites, left completely undisclosed.
items.evidence: oshb:Eccl.7.18 “ט֚וֹב אֲשֶׁ֣ר תֶּאֱחֹ֣ז בָּזֶ֔ה וְגַם מִזֶּ֖ה אַל תַּנַּ֣ח אֶת יָדֶ֑ךָ כִּֽי יְרֵ֥א אֱלֹהִ֖ים יֵצֵ֥א אֶת כֻּלָּֽם” (byte tier) opens on tov, and the tov-opener inventory lists Eccl.7.18 as the seventh of seven in-chapter sites the book's own device matrix names together as the series anaphora (7:1, 7:2, 7:3, 7:5, 7:8, 7:11, 7:18) -- a byte-true device at the row's own closing verse that the row's substrate-signal field flatly denies exists. The deictic "this / that" (zeh / mizeh) in 7:18 pointing back to 7:16 and 7:17's two admonitions still argues the verse cannot stand as a free member of that series on its own, so the admonition_unit call plausibly survives, but the undisclosed and directly inventory-contradicted claim is a genuine seam-warrant defect.
tier_citations: tov-opener inventory: 12 verses book-wide, 7 in ch.7 incl. Eccl.7.18 (7th site)

items.claim: single_saying is a properly disclosed operative-category deviation one verse outside the 7:1-14 zone: 7:19 is a self-contained comparative maxim sharing no content token with 7:18 or 7:20 and carrying no observation-frame marker.
items.evidence: oshb:Eccl.7.19 “הַֽחָכְמָ֖ה תָּעֹ֣ז לֶחָכָ֑ם מֵֽעֲשָׂרָה֙ שַׁלִּיטִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר הָי֖וּ בָּעִֽיר” (byte tier) shares no content root with oshb:Eccl.7.18's tov/yare close or oshb:Eccl.7.20's tzaddiq/chata vocabulary (“כִּ֣י אָדָ֔ם אֵ֥ין צַדִּ֖יק בָּאָ֑רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֥ר יַעֲשֶׂה טּ֖וֹב וְלֹ֥א יֶחֱטָֽא”); the verse is absent from both the raiti-observation and amarti-speech frame-marker inventories, matching the row's own claim that it lacks a narrative/observation marker; the deviation from the M parent's monologue_unit default is disclosed in one sentence as the operative-category law requires.

items.claim: admonition_unit correctly binds 7:20-7:22 as universal maxim plus its imperative corollary and grounding clause; the row's ketiv/qere disclosure at 7:22 is byte-accurate and its WEB and Hebrew quotes verify at byte tier.
items.evidence: oshb:Eccl.7.21 “גַּ֤ם לְכָל הַדְּבָרִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יְדַבֵּ֔רוּ אַל תִּתֵּ֖ן לִבֶּ֑ךָ אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹֽא תִשְׁמַ֥ע אֶֽת עַבְדְּךָ֖ מְקַלְלֶֽךָ” opens on gam ("also," byte tier), explicitly marking the verse as the corollary the row claims; oshb:Eccl.7.22 “כִּ֛י גַּם פְּעָמִ֥ים רַבּ֖וֹת יָדַ֣ע לִבֶּ֑ךָ אֲשֶׁ֥ר גַּם את אַתָּ֖ה קִלַּ֥לְתָּ אֲחֵרִֽים” (byte tier) carries the unpointed ketiv "et" immediately before its pointed qere "attah" ("you"), matching the single ketiv/qere note the inventory records at Eccl.7.22 (12 K/Q notes book-wide, single-witness WLC); the span shares no content root with 7:19's wisdom-value maxim before it and shifts to first-person nissiti/amarti at 7:23 after it, matching the amarti-speech inventory.
